bridge: LDPC-style decoder graph on a lag/check influence graph
novelty_signal: Strongest promoted bridge because the saved reframings and the probe both say honest locality at order 668 has to live on a sparse defect/check graph rather than on raw q/s adjacency.
validation_plan: Derive one sparse Tanner-like graph from exact lag or packet delta tables on the canonical 64-modular seed.
Benchmark weighted bit-flip, collective bit-flip, and graph-CA updates on that same graph, seed, and evaluation budget.
Instrument neighborhood size, message count, and active-node count to prove the bridge stays local.
Require exact reconstruction checks and a structured-family leakage audit before treating the bridge as more than a preconditioner.
risk: Sparsification may erase the real defect geometry and help only as a heuristic preconditioner.
If winning trajectories require global rescoring or dense collective flips, the locality claim collapses.
The graph can still reduce to optimizer-over-known-family if it hard-codes classical structured constraints.

bridge: Lag-residue CA on four 167-channels with explicit family-leakage audit
novelty_signal: Champion branch for the next pass because the verification summary and H2 gate both treat lag residues as the next honest local object once H1 is retired for principled locality failure.
validation_plan: Implement one lag-residue representation and exact delta tables back to sequence or q/s edits.
Run one matched non-CA lag-space control with the same seed, budget, restart count, and exact-hit gate.
Reject the branch if updates require whole-spectrum recomputation or if successful runs canonically collapse into known structured families.
Treat exact frontier improvement or exact-hit rate, not residual shrinkage alone, as the acceptance gate.
risk: Lag-space search can quietly collapse into Williamson, Turyn, Goethals-Seidel, cocyclic, or block-circulant structure.
Lag residues may still be fake-local if useful moves depend on nearly global information.
Cleaner state variables do not guarantee a workable actuator basis.

bridge: Warning-propagation side fields on the lag or decoder graph
novelty_signal: Held as the strongest auxiliary mechanism because LABS-style fields match the autocorrelation objective, but the fields should guide the CA rather than replace it.
validation_plan: Compute local lag-field summaries or warning messages on the same graph or lag representation used by H2 and the decoder-graph bridge.
Compare plain H2, plain warning propagation, and the hybrid under identical accounting.
Measure reversal rate, vote coherence, and exact-hit statistics instead of residual shrinkage alone.
risk: The method can collapse into message passing with a thin CA wrapper.
The same fields may help non-CA search equally, shrinking the CA-specific claim.
Field updates may smuggle in global information.

bridge: Composite-packet library as a bounded actuator upgrade
novelty_signal: Held, not promoted, because the probe identified composite packets as necessary for honest actuation, but this pass promotes H2 and the decoder graph rather than reopening H1.
validation_plan: Enumerate symmetry-safe composite packets and measure changed-lag footprint on the canonical seed.
Keep only low-splash packets with neutral or improving behavior.
Reuse the retained library inside H2 or decoder-graph benchmarks instead of widening standalone H1 sweeps.
risk: The library may still smuggle in known structure or benefit every baseline equally.
Packet enumeration can drift back toward whole-state search.
If no low-splash composites exist, the bridge does not rescue locality.

bridge: Current single-packet defect-syndrome CA on the q/s packet lattice
novelty_signal: Retired as an active frontier method after the matched kill test and the probe's fake-locality verdict.
validation_plan: Keep it only as a negative control when testing H2, the decoder graph, or future packet libraries.
Reuse its diffusion and neighborhood-freeze diagnostics as the baseline failure signature.
risk: No improving one-packet or two-packet moves exist on the canonical seed.
Support exceeds the seed support on every frontier restart.
Further tuning risks rebranding generic local search.

bridge: Generative spacetime row-emission CA rule search
novelty_signal: Retired for this pass because current evidence points to a representation pivot, while H3 still carries the highest prior-art overlap and the weakest frontier anchor.
validation_plan: Do not spend active budget in this pass.
Revisit only if H2 also fails for representation reasons and reduced-control defect-profile mimicry succeeds.
risk: High overlap with direct CA-construction literature.
Compact rule tables are poorly matched to the irregular 167-core frontier.
Easy drift into broad rule sweeps that do not answer the frontier bottleneck.
